answer: A new activity I have taken up recently is journaling, or writing down my thoughts each day. I started it a few months ago, after reading about its benefits for mental clarity and wellbeing. I bought a simple notebook from a stationery shop near my office, and I write in a mixture of Bengali and English, depending on what feels more natural. I began it because I often felt my mind was cluttered and I wanted a way to process my thoughts. Work had been particularly busy, and I was also thinking a lot about my future and whether to study abroad, so my head was full of unfinished worries. What I have discovered is that putting things down on paper is surprisingly [[therapeutic]]; it helps me make sense of my feelings. Each evening I spend a few minutes reflecting on my day, which has become a calming [[ritual]]. I usually write after dinner, when the house is quiet, sitting at my desk with a cup of tea. Honestly, I have found it far more [[beneficial]] than I expected. It has helped me become more [[self-aware]] and has noticeably reduced my stress. I also enjoy being able to look back and see how my thoughts have evolved over time; problems that felt huge a few months ago now seem quite small. I think it is a wonderfully simple yet [[rewarding]] practice. I intend to keep it up, as it has quickly become one of the most valuable parts of my daily routine.

followUps.q: Would you let anyone read your journal?
followUps.answer: Definitely not! It is completely private, which is exactly why I can be honest in it. My younger sister once tried to peek, and I have hidden it more carefully ever since.

followUps.q: Do you think journaling suits everyone?
followUps.answer: Not necessarily. Some people prefer talking things through or exercising to clear their minds. But I think anyone who tends to [[overthink]] would benefit from trying it for a few weeks.
